title: The Land Question
subtitle: A rebellion that grew out of rent, not theory.
objectives: Explain the causes of the Hukbalahap rebellion
Describe how the rebellion was ended
Explain why land reform kept returning

cards.title: The war ended. The land question did not
cards.text: Peasants who had fought the Japanese came home to the same landlords, the same rents and the same debts.

cards.title: A resistance army that did not disband
cards.text: The Hukbalahap began as an anti-Japanese guerrilla force in Central Luzon.
points: **The name means** the People's Army Against the Japanese.
**They had fought the occupation** effectively.
**After the war** many were treated as a threat, not as veterans.
**Some kept their weapons.**

cards.title: Tenancy, not ideology first
cards.text: The grievance was concrete before it was political.
points: **Tenant farmers** kept a small share of what they grew.
**Debts passed down** through families.
**Land reform had failed** in the 1930s and again after the war.
**Communist organisation came later**, onto a real grievance.

cards.title: Why a rebellion started
cards.text: Six steps, in order. Each one follows from the one before it.

question.text: The deepest cause of the Huk rebellion was…
question.explain: The political organising attached itself to a concrete grievance about land.

cards.title: A grievance with a physical meaning
cards.text: Tenancy is not an abstract arrangement. It decides whether a family eats.
points: **A bad harvest** still owed the same share.
**Debt carried into the next season**, and the next.
**Children worked** instead of attending school.
**That is what people took up arms about.**

question.text: The Huks began as a communist party militia.
question.explain: They began as an anti-Japanese guerrilla force. Communist organisation came later, onto an existing grievance.

cards.title: How the rebellion was ended
cards.text: Ramon Magsaysay, as Defence Secretary and then President, combined force with reform.
points: **He cleaned up the army** and stopped abuses against villagers.
**He offered land and amnesty** to those who surrendered.
**He made himself reachable**, famously opening the palace.
**The rebellion collapsed** by the mid-1950s.

question.text: Magsaysay's approach combined military pressure with…
question.explain: Force alone had failed. Addressing the grievance is what ended it.

cards.title: You cannot win this one by fighting only
cards.text: Strategy games model it: crush an uprising without fixing what caused it and it returns a few turns later.
points: **Military pressure alone** reduces numbers, not causes.
**Address the grievance** and recruitment dries up.
**Magsaysay did both at once**, which is why it stuck.
**The game is modelling** something real.

cards.title: Why the land question never closes
cards.text: Every administration this term promises land reform. Each one leaves some of it undone.
points: **The Commonwealth tried** and achieved little.
**Magsaysay resettled some families**, not most.
**Later presidents passed new laws.**
**Watch for it** in every week that follows.

cards.title: The thing it was all about
cards.alt: A golden rice field at harvest with cut sheaves stacked and a worn bolo knife laid across them
cards.text: Most of this harvest went to somebody the farmer had never met.

terms.def: The anti-Japanese guerrilla army that later rebelled.
Farming land owned by another for a share of the crop.
An official pardon offered to those who surrender.
Redistributing farmland or changing the terms of tenancy.

cards.title: What to remember
points: The Huks began as anti-Japanese guerrillas, not as a party militia.
The grievance was tenancy and debt, before it was ideology.
Magsaysay used force and reform together, and it worked.
Land reform remains the recurring unfinished business.

teacher.summary: Term 2 Week 6 Social Studies, the second week on the challenges of independence, and the one that explains why the period is unstable. The rebellion is taught cause-first: tenancy and debt were the grievance, and political organising arrived afterwards onto something already real. That ordering matters, because the opposite framing makes the rebellion look imported. Magsaysay's solution is given in full (stopping army abuses, offering land and amnesty alongside military pressure) since the lesson is that force alone had already been tried and failed. Land reform is explicitly flagged as the thread to watch in every remaining week.
discussion: Why did the Huks not disband after the war?
Why does land reform appear in every decade?
extension: Find out what crops are grown near your family's province and who owns that land.
Trace land reform laws from 1935 to today.
misconceptions: That the Huks were always a communist militia.
That the rebellion was purely ideological.
That Magsaysay solved it by force alone.
